On 30 December 2019, Wuhan Centres for Disease Prevention and Control (Wuhan CDC) issued emergency warnings to local hospitals about a number of mysterious "pneumonia" cases discovered in the city in the previous week.[4] On the same day, Li, who worked at the Central Hospital of Wuhan, received an internal diagnostic report of a suspected severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) patient from other doctors, which he in turn shared with his Wuhan University alumni through a WeChat group.
> *   **Li:** There are 7 confirmed cases of SARS at Huanan Seafood Market.
> *   **Li:** They are being isolated in the emergency department of our hospital's Houhu Hospital District.
> *   **Someone:** Be careful, our class group chat got shut down.
> *   **Li:** The latest news is, it has been confirmed that they are coronavirus infections, but the exact virus is being subtyped.
> *   **Li:** Don't circulate the information outside of this group, tell your family and loved ones to take precautions.
> *   **Li:** In 1937, coronaviruses were first isolated from chicken...
The letter of admonition issued by the Wuhan Police Bureau (translation) ordering Li to stop "spreading rumors" about SARS, co-signed by Li and two officers.
Li uploaded it to his Sina Weibo account.

By early June 2020, five other doctors had died from COVID-19 in the Wuhan hospital, now called the "whistleblower hospital".[17] Hu Weifeng, a urologist and a coworker of Li, was the sixth doctor of the hospital to die from the virus on 2 June 2020, after four months of hospitalization.
